events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Visibility below a half mile in dense fog.

* WHERE...Espanola Valley, Far Northwest Highlands Including Dulce,
Santa Fe Metro Area, Tusas Mountains Including Chama, Northeast
Highlands Including Las Vegas, and Union County Including Clayton.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM MDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility will make driving conditions hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...I-25 will be impacted from La Bajada Hill
northeastward through Santa Fe, as well as the Santa Fe Relief
Route, and Highway 285 northward through Espanola.  I-25 will also
be impacted in the Las Vegas area.

events.region: Guam Coastal Waters; Rota Coastal Waters
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Typhoon In-fa will approach the far northern CNMI late Friday and
into the weekend. Winds and seas will increase Friday afternoon ahead
of the approaching typhoon, potentially exceeding hazardous levels
to small craft by late Friday night, with seas approaching 10 feet.
Mariners are urged to remain weather aware over the coming days.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Tinian Coastal Waters; Saipan Coastal Waters
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Typhoon In-fa will approach the far northern CNMI late Friday and
into the weekend. Winds and seas will sharply increase starting early
Friday ahead of the approaching typhoon, quickly exceeding hazardous
levels to small craft early on Friday. Seas of 10 to 15 feet are
expected to develop in the coastal of Tinian and Saipan. Although,
sustained winds are not expected to reach tropical-storm force at
this time, tropical-storm force gusts are possible. Mariners are
urged to remain weather aware over the coming days.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Southeastern Dallam County in the panhandle of Texas...
Northeastern Hartley County in the panhandle of Texas...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Low-water crossings are inundated
with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 654 AM CDT, local law enforcement reported flooding in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring. Between 3 and 4
inches of rain have fallen.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Dalhart and Hartley.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
